lesson.text: Quick memory: is C, E, G major or minor? (Major: C up to E is 4 semitones.) Today: chords, notes played together.
A chord is three or more notes played at the same time. Listen: C, E and G together make the chord of C major.
Build a chord by skipping letters: start on its root, skip a letter, take the next, skip one, take the next. From C: C, (skip D) E, (skip F) G.
Chords have names. The C major chord is C, E and G; the F major chord is F, A and C; the G major chord is G, B and D. Minor chords have a small m: Am, Dm, Em.
Worked example: the A minor chord is A, C and E. From A up to C is 3 semitones, so the chord sounds minor. Its short name is Am.
A chord pattern: lots of songs move C, F, G, then back to C. Listen: each chord lasts two beats.
Play a chord's notes one after another and you get a broken chord, also called an arpeggio. Guitarists and harpists often play chords this way.
Try it in the world: on any keyboard, play C E G, then F A C, then G B D, then C E G again. You have played a chord pattern! Next: how songs are built.

exercises.prompt: Which notes make the C major chord?
exercises.hint: Start on C, then skip a letter, take one, skip, take one.
exercises.explain: From C, skip D to E, skip F to G: the C major chord is C, E and G.

exercises.prompt: A chord is three or more notes played at the same time.
exercises.hint: Think of C, E and G together.
exercises.explain: True: a chord is notes played together, like C, E and G.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this chord major or minor?
exercises.hint: Bright, or darker? Listen to the middle note.
exercises.explain: It is G, B and D: 4 semitones from G to B, so it is major.

exercises.prompt: Match each chord name to its notes.
exercises.hint: Start on the name's letter, and skip letters.
exercises.explain: C is C, E, G; F is F, A, C; G is G, B, D; and Am is A, C, E.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Did you hear one note, or a chord?
exercises.hint: Could you hear more than one pitch at the same time?
exercises.explain: Three notes sounded together, F, A and C: a chord.

exercises.prompt: Which chord is on the stave?
exercises.hint: The lowest note names the chord. Then count the semitones up to the middle note.
exercises.explain: D, F and A: D is the root, and D up to F is 3 semitones, so it is D minor.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this chord major or minor?
exercises.hint: Does it sound bright, or darker?
exercises.explain: It is E, G and B: 3 semitones from E to G, so it is minor.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many chords did you hear?
exercises.hint: Count each time the sound changes and all the notes start together.
exercises.explain: C, F, G, then C again: 4 chords, each lasting two beats.

exercises.prompt: A song plays the chords C, F, G and C, each for 2 beats. How many beats is that?
Put the notes of the F major chord in order, from the bottom up.
exercises.hint: Start on F, then skip a letter each time.
exercises.explain: F, skip G, A, skip B, C: F, A and C.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Was it a broken chord or a chord played together?
exercises.hint: Did the notes start one after another, or all at once?
exercises.explain: The notes G, B and D came one after another: a broken chord.

exercises.prompt: The G major chord is G, B and D.
exercises.hint: Start on G and skip letters.
exercises.explain: True: from G, skip A to B, skip C to D.

exercises.prompt: Which chord is on the stave?
exercises.hint: The lowest note names the chord. Count the semitones up to the middle note.
exercises.explain: E, G and B: E up to G is 3 semitones, so it is E minor.

exercises.prompt: Which melody note fits best over a C major chord?
exercises.hint: A melody note that is in the chord sounds settled.
exercises.explain: E is one of the chord's own notes (C, E, G), so it blends. F and D sit right next to chord notes and rub against them, and B clashes with the C.

exercises.prompt: Listen to this broken chord. Is it major or minor?
exercises.hint: Listen to the second note: how far above the first?
exercises.explain: It is A, C and E: A up to C is 3 semitones, so it is minor.

exercises.prompt: How many semitones is it from F up to A, in the F major chord?
exercises.hint: Count every key from F to A, black keys too.
exercises.explain: F to F sharp, G, G sharp, A: 4 semitones, which makes the chord major.

exercises.prompt: Which stave shows the C major chord?
exercises.hint: Read each chord's notes from the bottom: C major is C, E and G.
exercises.explain: The chord on middle C's ledger line with E and G above it is C major.

exercises.prompt: Listen. These two chords are the same.
exercises.hint: Listen to the middle note of each chord.
exercises.explain: False: the first is C major (C, E, G) and the second C minor (C, E flat, G).

exercises.prompt: Sort the chords: major or minor?
exercises.hint: Count the semitones from the root up to the middle note: 4 is major, 3 is minor.
exercises.explain: Major: C to E, F to A and G to B are 4 semitones each. Minor: A to C, D to F and E to G are 3 semitones each.
